title: Linguistic Calibration of Long-Form Generations
abstract: Defines linguistic calibration for long-form generation in terms of whether generated confidence statements enable calibrated downstream probabilistic judgments. A supervised-plus-reinforcement-learning approach produces long-form answers with calibrated uncertainty expressions, with automated and human evaluation and tests under substantial domain shift.

title: Claim-Level Confidence Calibration for Reliable Decision Making with Large Language Models
abstract: Studies calibrated confidence for individual factual claims rather than whole responses. It combines atomic claim decomposition, consistency and self-verification signals, and post-hoc calibration, enabling low-confidence claims to be selectively sent for retrieval or human review.

title: Only Say What You Know: Calibration-Aware Generation for Long-Form Factuality
abstract: Proposes Calibration-Aware Generation, which separates exploratory reasoning from commitment to final claims. Intermediate information receives calibrated reliability estimates, allowing the model to prioritize reliable content and avoid committing uncertain material in long-form generation.

title: Program-Verifiable Evaluation for Temporal QA: Metrics for Evidence Validity
abstract: Separates answer correctness from the temporal validity of cited evidence in time-sensitive QA. It introduces program-verifiable metrics for evidence freshness and an oracle-answer diagnostic that can expose temporally invalid evidence even when the final answer is held correct.

title: Minimal Evidence Group Identification for Claim Verification
abstract: Formalizes the identification of minimal groups of evidence pieces that collectively provide full support for a claim. The formulation explicitly distinguishes full from partial support and allows multiple alternative evidence groups, making it relevant to evidence-completeness evaluation for multi-source claims.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Treats evidence sufficiency as a set-level property in selective RAG rather than equating passage relevance with adequate support. Its verifier aggregates evidence coverage, support strength, conflict, and uncertainty and permits answering only when the retrieved evidence set is judged sufficient.

title: MSRS: Evaluating Multi-Source Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces benchmarks for retrieval and long-form synthesis when required information is distributed across multiple sources and no individual source is sufficient. The evaluation separates retrieval effectiveness from the ability to integrate and synthesize evidence across sources, including an oracle-retrieval setting.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
abstract: Develops adaptive conformal inference for sequential data whose distribution changes over time in unknown ways. Instead of assuming exchangeability, the method adapts the conformal miscoverage level online and targets long-run coverage under distribution shift.

title: When Can Conformal Risk Control Certify LLM Outputs? Bounds, Impossibility, and Adaptation for Structured Generation
abstract: Studies when conformal risk control can certify structured language-model outputs and derives limits showing when a target risk requires abstention because base risk is too high. It also examines adaptation under cross-dataset shift, connecting statistical risk guarantees to selective generation.

title: DEER: A Benchmark for Evaluating Deep Research Agents on Expert Report Generation
abstract: Evaluates evidence-based expert report generation with an expert-developed multidimensional rubric taxonomy and report-wide claim verification. Its verification architecture checks both cited and uncited claims, assesses evidence quality, and exposes logical-completeness failures that ordinary citation-presence measures can miss.

title: Auto-ARGUE: LLM-Based Report Generation Evaluation
abstract: Introduces an automated LLM-based implementation of the ARGUE framework for evaluating long-form citation-backed reports. Evaluation on the TREC 2024 NeuCLIR report-generation pilot shows good system-level correlation with human judgments and operationalizes report completeness, accuracy, and citation-oriented diagnostics.

title: Self-Evaluation Improves Selective Generation in Large Language Models
abstract: Studies selective generation for open-ended model outputs by reformulating self-evaluation into token-prediction tasks. It compares self-evaluation scoring strategies, including an explicit none-of-the-above option, and evaluates their ability to identify when generation should be withheld on TruthfulQA and TL;DR.

title: LoVeC: Reinforcement Learning for Better Verbalized Confidence in Long-Form Generation
abstract: Trains language models with reinforcement learning to append numerical confidence estimates to individual statements during long-form generation. Evaluation on long-form QA examines free-form and iterative confidence tagging and reports improved calibration and cross-domain generalization.

title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness
abstract: Targets the completeness side of long-form factuality rather than only precision of generated claims. A structured meta-rubric represents required content, importance, open-ended sets, processes, and relations, then compiles these requirements into binary checks scored by an LLM judge; the evidence-backed rubrics are verified by expert human annotators.

title: Selective Generation for Controllable Language Models
abstract: Develops selective-generation algorithms for language models that control a generation risk defined using textual entailment while retaining useful output. The method provides statistical control over false discoveries in generated sequences and studies supervised and semi-supervised settings.

title: Validating LLM-as-a-Judge Systems under Rating Indeterminacy
abstract: Shows that validation of LLM judges can be biased when human rating tasks admit several reasonable labels but evaluation collapses them to a single forced-choice gold rating. It develops a validation framework using response-set ratings and evaluates the approach across multiple real-world rating tasks and commercial models.

title: Reducing Conversational Agents’ Overconfidence Through Linguistic Calibration
abstract: Studies whether free-form dialogue agents express verbal confidence or doubt in proportion to their factual correctness. It shows substantial miscalibration in existing agents and improves linguistic calibration by incorporating predicted correctness into controllable generation.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Think Through Uncertainty: Improving Long-Form Generation Factuality via Reasoning Calibration
abstract: Introduces a claim-aware reasoning protocol in which long-form outputs are decomposed into atomic claims carrying explicit confidence estimates. A multi-stage training pipeline aligns confidence with claim correctness, and the resulting confidence is used for selective abstention from uncertain claims.

title: Agreement is overrated: A plea for correlation to assess human evaluation reliability
abstract: Examines reliability assessment in human evaluation of natural-language generation and argues that inter-annotator agreement alone is inadequate in the presence of legitimate linguistic variability. It recommends considering correlation together with agreement and supports the argument through a survey and case studies.

title: Can LLMs Evaluate Complex Attribution in QA? Automatic Benchmarking using Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Introduces CAQA for evaluating complex evidence attribution with fine-grained attribution categories and deliberately subtle attribution differences. It benchmarks 25 automatic evaluators, compares them with human evaluators, and studies evaluators fine-tuned on the benchmark.

title: Do LLMs Know When Evidence is Insufficient? An Evidence Sufficiency Benchmark for Answer-Abstention Calibration in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Benchmarks answer-versus-abstain behavior under full, partial, irrelevant, absent, and conflicting retrieved evidence, directly testing whether RAG systems distinguish insufficient evidence from supported answerability.

title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
abstract: Introduces SciFact, where systems retrieve scientific abstracts, determine whether evidence supports or refutes a claim, and identify rationale spans justifying the decision.

title: When Benchmarks Age: Temporal Misalignment through Large Language Model Factuality Evaluation
abstract: Examines temporal misalignment in factuality benchmarks, showing why factuality evaluation must account for benchmark age and whether facts and evidence remain current at evaluation time.

title: ReproHum #0892-01: The painful route to consistent results: A reproduction study of human evaluation in NLG
abstract: Reproduces an NLG human-evaluation study and analyzes difficulties in obtaining consistent judgments, providing empirical evidence about protocol sensitivity and evaluation reliability.

title: ChronoFact: Timeline-based Temporal Fact Verification
abstract: Frames temporal fact verification around timelines so claims can be evaluated against evidence valid at relevant times, rather than treating factual truth as temporally invariant.

title: Runtime Verification of Temporal Properties over Out-of-order Data Streams
abstract: Studies verification of temporal properties when observations arrive out of order, providing transferable machinery for reasoning about changing state and late evidence in event streams.

title: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Abstractive Text Summarization
abstract: Introduces a source-grounded factual-consistency model that jointly predicts consistency and extracts a supporting source span and an inconsistent summary span, enabling localized evidence for factuality judgments.

title: Attributed Question Answering: Evaluation and Modeling for Attributed Large Language Models
abstract: Defines attributed question answering, where answers must be accompanied by evidence sources that support them, and develops human and automatic evaluation of answer quality and attribution.

title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents
abstract: Evaluates source attribution in deep-research outputs by checking whether cited sources work, contain relevant material, and actually substantiate generated factual claims rather than merely appearing plausible.

title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
abstract: Benchmarks LLM citation verifiers against human-reviewed and adjudicated judgments of source relevance and factual support, emphasizing false-positive and false-negative behavior rather than raw judge agreement alone.

title: Formal and functional assessment of the pyramid method for summary content evaluation
abstract: Evaluates the reliability and discriminative power of Pyramid annotations across multiple summarization evaluations, including inter-annotator reliability and consistency of system rankings.

title: Agreement Metrics for LLM-as-Judge Evaluation: What to Report and Why
abstract: Analyzes agreement metrics for LLM-as-judge evaluation and discusses what different measures reveal, including treatment of judge abstentions and the need to report coverage alongside agreement.

title: Augmenting Human Evaluation with LLM Judges: How Many Human Reviews Do You Need?
abstract: Studies hybrid evaluation designs that combine LLM judges with retained human review, focusing on how much human validation is needed rather than treating model judgments as an unvalidated gold standard.

title: SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
abstract: Revisits natural-language-inference approaches to detecting whether summaries contain statements unsupported by their source documents and meta-evaluates them across factual-consistency datasets.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
abstract: Introduces ALCE for long-form generation with citations and evaluates citation quality, including whether cited passages entail generated claims and whether claims that require support are adequately cited.

title: Better than Random: Reliable NLG Human Evaluation with Constrained Active Sampling
abstract: Studies sampling reliability in NLG human evaluation and proposes constrained active sampling to make limited human-review budgets more representative and stable across system comparisons.

title: How Can We Know When Language Models Know? On the Calibration of Language Models for Question Answering
abstract: Studies whether language-model probabilities in question answering correspond to empirical correctness and investigates techniques for improving confidence calibration.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
